sentences.text: Hey, Andy.
Hi, Alex.
How you doing?
Yeah, I'm good, thanks.
How are you?
Yeah, not too bad once I just make sure everything's on my earpods.
You hear me okay?
Yeah, okay.
You loud and clear?
Yeah, all good.
Good stuff.
Long time.
I see.
How you doing?
That's been a while.
Yeah, yeah.
Well, good, thank you.
Yeah, yeah, I mean, it's a mix of both really, clients looking to sell and other buy side clients as well.
We've done about three or four deals the last couple of months, so been busy both buy and sell side.
We sold a great company from Israel.
We just bought one in the UK and we're just about to buy the second with the same client in California and then a third again in the UK with the same clients.
They've been exceedingly busy.
That sounds fun.
Is that lots of travel for you then or is it not too bad?

Well, we have done a lot of travel, but, yeah, I mean it's all, it's all pretty much from a screen most of the time, but, yeah, we've been in the US for six months, the second half of last year, me and my family, and we got back at the start of this year and just been in the UK mostly.
But, yeah, I mean, I've seen various emails about your like your accelerators where you invite people in to join a buy and build accelerator.
How's that sort of things going?
Yeah, really good.
Really good.
We're just about to do a second run of it, so, yeah, it's basically to fill a gap in the market.
So we work with obviously a lot of buyers and sellers, but there's a large group of people that we speak to and they book calls with us, but they're not ready to sell.
They don't really know tons about M and A and they don't really know, they don't really have a strategy.
I've been getting this for years and it's the same thing.
It's like we're going to sell in two or three years, but there's no real strategy there.
It's just organic growth that they're looking at.
But most agencies that we speak to, they just kind of plateau and we'll speak to them three or four years later and it's the, the same business or worse.

So really the accelerator is about how to fill that gap those two years instead of hoping it's actually to have a good strategy and grow the business, either just through making some changes to the business and the way that you run it or to then go on a buying spree and make at least one or two acquisitions.
Nice.
I mean, that could be.
I mean, that's sort of what I want to speak to you about, really.
So, I mean, should I just kind of run through why I reached out and kind of like, put in this call?
Yeah, definitely.
What have you been up to?
Yeah.
And what are you thinking?
It'd be great to know more.
Yeah.
So long.
Long story short is we've grown nicely, grown really nicely over the last couple of years.
Not, not like explosive, but like about 25% this year, about 30% last year.
After the jungle conversations, in the end, we all backed out and just didn't feel right.
It was a point in time where we basically decided, okay, what are we actually doing with this business?
Where are we going, what's the plan?
And basically we realized that we had to properly invest in the business to get to the next level.
So, 1st, 18 months from there.
So that was most of 2023.
Kind of about halfway through 2024 was all about, let's do a rebrand, let's get a nice office, let's work on our proposition.
Let's bring in the FD, the MD, the marketing director, let's change our tools.
Let's basically get ourselves on the radar to basically level up as a business.
And we brought in some really good people from, we are social, we've gotten people from various different places.
It's invested properly in the business.
And all in all, I would say it.
It's working.
It's working, but, and I suppose it's working in that the work is a lot better.
We are attracting some really great rfps, we're winning some really good work.
Our reputation is growing and that's all well and good.
And we're happy with that.
We're happy with 20% growth.
We've taken a small profit hit, but ultimately we're still profitable.
We should do about just about five in turnover this year and sort of about 16 17% EBITDA.
So all in all, we're in a good place.

However, the but is very much in line with what you said there, which is like, that's all great, but it doesn't excite us and we're worried about plateauing and we want to basically make a move in our market.
The social space feels like it's moving forward really fast and there's a bunch of really good agencies and we are bored in a nice muscle way of pure organic growth.
It's good, it makes sense, it's worked.
But we've got a chairman.
Now, who actually, you may know, you may have come across him, a guy called John Smith, who was back with jungle creations back in the day from the BBC.
Isn't he exactly a BBC guy?
Yeah, I went to lunch with him with the guy from jungle not so probably about a year ago now.
Two years.
That makes sense.
So John's going to come on and we spent sort of a couple of months just sort of plotting and planning and like, what are we going to do?
Are we going to grow organically and see, are we going to move international?
Are we going to move into a different vertical, like social publishing, whatever it might be?
And of all the different things that we weighed up, essentially, we settled on acquisition, buy and build tuck ins, whatever you want to call them.
We basically feel like the market is really primed for us to grow through some strategic acquisitions, which obviously is your thing, so don't need to explain how that kind of why that makes sense.

We think it's a really good opportunity, not only because the fact that there's lots of struggling markets in that kind of like mid struggling agencies in that mid tier, but also it's just, it's something which entrepreneurially, Max, and Max, my business partner and I want to do, we're interested by.
So we are actively doing it.
We've got the right things in place.
We are essentially making the strongest signal to the market of what we're looking for and why, and basically looking to get going with it, really.
So I guess I want to speak to you on a couple of levels.
First, one is broadly, do you know anything on the market?
And I can talk through our criteria in a moment.
B, how can you help and see, is that anything to do with the accelerator and could that be relevant for, for someone like us?
And that's the long and the short of it.
Does that, does that all make sense?
Yeah, that's great.
So I would say the accelerator probably doesn't make sense for you guys, given that you've got John in place already.
Quite a lot of what we do, somebody like John would be able to, is already doing.

I mean, it's about getting bums on seats, getting the right bums on the right seats and getting the bus going in the right direction and having a big sort of, you know, a big strategy, a big goal that you need to reach and then, and then sort of a twelve to, well, twelve is really quick, but twelve to 24 months sort of strategy to get there.
And basically you're crushing, like, you know, four or five years growth into that twelve to 24 months and that's what the accelerator is doing and that's what John will be doing.
I mean, it's all about the knowledge and having the balls to do these acquisitions.
And I mean, I say having the balls and it literally is down to that.
A lot of people will get the knowledge, but it's, you know, it's a big step to do it.
And having John on board or having us on board as part of the accelerator is, is that step really, and just having somebody that knows what they're doing on board.
So I don't think that's the way that we can help you.
Obviously, we do list companies that are for sale, and there's potentially one or two in there that might fit what you're looking for.
But I would say probably the best way that we can work with you is working on the buy side.
And again, this is about sort of crushing three years down into sort of a six month project where we were able to really accelerate and speed up.
Really, it's a volume game.
So what happens is guys like you will go to the market.

Obviously you've got a full time job doing what you're doing, and you will come across, there will be a lot of agencies that will come across your desk for sale, but really you need to accelerate that sort of three or four a week if you want to get an acquisition done within six to twelve months, because it just is, it's mostly a game of saying no to stuff.
And obviously one a month is not going to get you where you need to be.
Most deals for fall over.
I think the statistic is 110 acquisition.
So where an offer is made, they don't close.
So you just need to be making a lot of offers to get deals closed.
And that's how we come in as a partner.
We're able to just scale up what you're doing already.
We work to whatever the targets are that you're looking for.
And we're bringing in two or three of those every single week screened.
And we're just constantly doing that for 3456 months until we get the right fit.
Somebody is in the right place at the right time, and you're making a couple of offers every couple of months at least, and then one of them is going to close.
I mean, it's just statistics basically.
So that's what we do and that's what we're working with our clients to do on the buy side.
Nice.
We're doing that globally.
Amazing.
And you tend to source off market deals then or a mixture of off market, on market basically.
No, on market really.
I mean some stuff we might come across will be on the market, but it's, we're contacting everybody directly that fit your criteria.
So, you know, we're going out to a huge pool.
We've got 130,000 agencies in our database, you know, and within those we're targeting, you know, businesses that match what it is that you need to acquire to complete your strategy.
So we're doing that.
And then on top of that as well, my team will be, you know, just constantly researching and reaching out to new agencies that aren't in our database.
I mean it's pretty, it's pretty comprehensive.
Anyway, we've got pretty much everybody in there, but if we haven't, for one reason or another, we're adding them all the time.
So yeah, we'll find what it is that you want.
We'll get those conversations started and then bring them on a weekly basis to the table for you to talk to and see if you like them.
That's really interesting.
It sounds very relevant in terms of do you have a minimum size of deal where it starts to make sense whereby your fees and your ways of working make sense or does it vary?
Well obviously the bigger deals make better sense to us because it's the same amount of work, to be honest with you.
Yeah.
Doesn't really change.
If anything, the smaller companies are a little bit more work because, you know, there's usually a big personality involved and much less experience.

So obviously there's kind of an educational curve you have to take them through, whereas companies that are bigger, quite often the principal will have had some experience in m and a before and there's just less to sort of educate.
But yeah, I mean in terms of what size makes sense, I mean we work on all sorts of deals to be honest with you.
We just, like I said, we just closed the couple with one client, which is some investors based in Florida.
But we're also working with a company that acquires small WordPress businesses.
And most of them are tiny, we're just stacking them up, buying them cheap sort of thing.
Um, you know, WordPress developers and hosting companies and there's millions of them on the planet, so.
And they're all tiny.
We're pretty much one man band.
So um.
So we work on all sorts of.
Stuff that makes, makes perfect sense.
Yeah, because I suppose, I mean look, we'll, we'll figure this out.
Logic, logic is telling us to do something kind of like small to mid size and by that I basically mean kind of between.
Between one and 2 million turnover.
Just to sort of start off like 1015 people taking on some good clients, take on a speciality.
We got our criteria, which obviously, I can share with you.
Logic says, start there, integrate that well, do it properly.
But the other day, we also know that bigger stuff can happen sometimes.
And if there was something which felt more like a merger of a larger company, then we're kind of open to that.
Or buying something bigger, which is kind of off market, even if it is sort of similar size to us.
And we're about just under 60 people, so we're open minded, basically.
Yeah.
I guess there's two ways to look at that.
The thing is, any deal kind of takes the same amount of effort, I think, with John on board as well.
I mean, a big part of it is just being able to get your story right and making an attractive home for somebody to end up in.

And if you can't convince the seller that you are, that maybe they might think you're too young or the company's too new or you're not big enough to acquire them, then that will obviously slow things down.
But, yeah, that's part of the game, basically, is getting the company in a place where it looks like it can acquire pretty much anything.
But obviously, if you make that small first acquisition, not only does it bump up the size of you, it gives you a track record, and then the next deal is easier and can be larger.
We've done a tiny one, which is at least part of the very initial story, I suppose.
We did an Aqua hire last year.
We took on.
Took on a few people, seven or eight clients, and kind of did.
It did an integration, at least.
So we've got a little bit of that story, but I think you're absolutely right.
Like, the numbers would work if we took on, let's say, 1.5 million turnover and took an extra 15 people.
Then it bumps up the numbers quite nicely.
It starts to make us get towards that sort of 100 mark, that 10 million mark, which is what we're aiming for.
Yeah, I think it would be probably the easiest way to go.
It gives you the experience and then confidence on the next one.

And if that puts you in a position where you're able to do an acquisition where somebody is the same size or larger, then that kind of gives you the confidence to be in the driving seat for that deal.
Yeah.
Which is great.
Okay, perfect.
That's really good to know.
And then my other question is, do you or do you have any thoughts around, let's just say struggling agencies.
Right.
We hear about a left, right and center.
Every job posting we have at the moment is somebody who's being made redundant or an agency struggling and often quite impressive names, quite decent sort of decent reputation businesses.
Do you recommend looking at the kind of the.
On the way to distressed businesses or the kind of struggling businesses?
Or is that.
Again, I know turnarounds are a different kettle of fish versus decent businesses, but what do you think about that?
I think it could be a huge distraction.
If these businesses were going to work, then they should work.
But sometimes they have easy problems to fix.

Quite often they're not marketing themselves properly and they have experienced teams and fairly good relationships with clients, but it's difficult to value them and they will feel that they're valued at a certain amount.
And there's just.
I mean, if a company is losing money or it's breaking even, the value basically is zero.
So I think that's the tricky part, is being able to get those deals done.
But I think if you come into them and can negotiate well, they can be quite effective.

Yeah, I mean, I'd say it's definitely not a no, but I don't really see how they can offer, bottom line, sort of tangible growth on day one, the next day after the deal is closed, I mean, it is a certain amount of work to turn those around, but each to their own.

I think I've seen a lot of companies successfully do that and I've seen others that have done multiple deals in that market and they're just running shit little agencies better than somebody else was.
It really does depend.
Every company is different and every opportunity is different.
So, yeah, I think it's just good to talk to everybody and see whether.
That makes perfect sense.
Cool.
I mean, that's not, that's our situation.

So again, obviously, I'm sure you've got plenty of opportunities and sounds like you're quite busy, but I mean, happy to hear what kind of opportunities you have available in terms of, like, working together and in whatever format is best for you.
Yeah, well, like I said, I think the best way for us both to work together is for us to work on a buy side search for you.
I mean, I would just.
In terms of just looking at it as a six month project where we were able to bring probably three to five years worth of searching on your own, just into a six month process.
It's all about scaling up your efforts.
Whatever you're working on right now, we will do that like ten times faster.
So the way that we work is it's a retained model, so it's four k a month.
And then we take one and a half percent on the deal as well.
So, you know, most of our clients are getting, are raising capital from banks or from private equity.
And it's fairly common for the bankers to get a percentage on the deal.
So it's not usually complicated to add our fees in.
Pretty straightforward.
So that's the way we work.
Yeah.
In terms of stuff coming up, I mean, I can get you signed up onto our agency's mailing list if you're not already.
I think if you're already getting my emails, you possibly are in there.

And we send out listings when they list new and otherwise just have a check of the website if you've missed an announcement for a new list and just have a quick look and see whether anything new is up that fits what you're looking for.
Okay, perfect.
Yeah, that sounds good to me.
Okay, cool.
That's kind of what I need to know.
Really?
That will make sense.
Okay, cool.
So, I mean, in terms of where you are, obviously you guys have started the process already.
I'm sure John's advising you of what you need to do.
Is it something that you're looking to do?
Have a, you know, sort of by, by side search going on as well or are you happy to continue?
At the moment?
Yeah, I mean, yes, essentially we're pulling a couple of different levers just to see what kind of stuff's out there.
I think, as you say, like, I think the realization is that to see you say no to a lot and need to see a lot, to say no to a lot of things are kind of quite aware of that at the moment.
There's a couple of opportunities that sort of just fell into our lap.
So we're, we're looking at those at the moment just to see kind of what, what's working and what's interesting there.
But realistically, we want to push this forward.
We want to get something done early.
Well, h 120 25.
So time is of the essence and a reasonable fee to see a flow of agencies is pretty reasonable.
So basically, step one was to reach out to a couple of people we know in the market who do this kind of thing just to see what's going on, basically.
Okay, brilliant.
All right.
Well, I'll send you an email just with that summarized.
And if I don't hear back from you, I'll chase you up in a month or so.
I'm sure it'll take you a bit to sort of finish those conversations that you're having, but, yeah, it becomes quite a lot of work trying to find new deals all the time.
So I'm sure you'll come knocking if it's the right fit for you.
I think that sounds exactly right.
Thanks for explaining everything.
Good to catch up and I'll look up your emails.
Yeah, no.
Good to hear from you.
Good to hear you're doing so well.
No, thanks.
You too.
I'll speak to you soon.
Yep.
Enjoy the rest of your day.

summary.overview: In the recent Business Development and Strategy Discussion meeting between Alex Bodini and Andy Day, they explored potential growth avenues through acquisitions. Alex reported a significant 25-30% growth in his company over the last two years, supported by a recent rebranding and strategic hires, with a projected turnover of around 5 million and an EBITDA of 16-17%. Discussing acquisition strategies, Andy highlighted his firm's services in sourcing both on-market and off-market deals, recommending that Alex focus on acquiring smaller agencies with a turnover of 1-2 million and a workforce of 10-15 people, while also weighing the pros and cons of acquiring struggling firms. They established action items, with Alex tasked to review follow-up materials and consider Andy’s search services, while Andy will provide a summary email and ensure Alex’s inclusion in agency listings. Both have plans to continue the conversation, with follow-ups scheduled in the coming month.
summary.short_summary: During the Business Development and Strategy Discussion, Alex Bodini and Andy Day explored acquisition strategies to fuel growth for Alex's company, which has seen a remarkable 25-30% increase over the past two years. Alex shared insights on his company's recent rebranding efforts and strategic hires, projecting a turnover of around 5 million and an EBITDA of 16-17%. Andy detailed his firm's capabilities in sourcing both on-market and off-market deals, advising Alex to target smaller agencies with a turnover of 1-2 million and a workforce of 10-15 people. They discussed the pros and cons of acquiring struggling firms as well. Action items were established, with Alex set to review follow-up materials and consider Andy's services, while Andy will summarize their discussion and ensure Alex is included in agency listings. They agreed to have follow-ups in the coming month to continue their conversation.
